intro: Regensburg protects its trees one at a time, by number. A plane 31 metres tall shares a lawn with a medieval gate tower in the Herzogspark, another holds a street corner in Prebrunn, and a third grows on a Roman market place. Over the Steinerne Bruecke, two protected chestnut groups stand a few doors apart in Stadtamhof. Those five are one free afternoon on foot. Further out stand a village-centre oak in Wutzlhofen and four oaks in Unterisling. The giant is 8 km south: an oak 7.20 metres round with a Madonna in its trunk.
meta_description: Eight protected trees in and near Regensburg: a plane by a medieval gate tower, chestnuts over the Stone Bridge, and an oak with a Madonna in its trunk.
question_answer: The oldest tree inside Regensburg on this page is the Wutzlhofen Oak, on the village green of Wutzlhofen in the north-east of the city. The ordinance that protected it in 1994 put it at about 180 to 200 years, which carries forward to roughly 210 to 230 today; that is a round official figure, not a ring count. Next comes the plane in the Herzogspark, put at 150 to 200 years by the tree register baumkunde.de and at 200 by a photographer's caption from 2022. The other five city entries, two more planes, two chestnut groups and the four Unterisling oaks, are protected without a date between them: Regensburg's natural monument register records what is designated and when, almost never how old it is. Any one of them could be older. Outside the city the answer changes: the Bildeiche, an oak 8 km south near Obertraubling, is put at roughly 350 years by Rainer Lippert's estimate, and its trunk is 7.20 metres round. If you know of a planting record for any of the city trees, tell us and this page changes.
question_meta: Inside the city, the oldest tree here is the Wutzlhofen Oak at roughly 210 to 230 years; the Bildeiche oak 8 km south is put at about 350.
question_context:
Regensburg protects individual trees rather than dating them. Its natural monument ordinance gives each tree or group a number, a street and a date, and usually no age, so five of the seven city entries here carry no figure. The exceptions are the Wutzlhofen Oak, put at 180 to 200 years by its own 1994 ordinance, and the Herzogspark plane, which the tree register baumkunde.de puts at 150 to 200 and measured at 6.2 metres round and 31 metres tall in 2024.

Five of the city trees are easy to see in one go. The Herzogspark plane and the Singrün corner plane are five minutes apart in Prebrunn. The plane at the Alter Kornmarkt stands in the UNESCO-listed centre, on a square used for trade since Roman times. The two chestnut groups are over the Steinerne Bruecke in Stadtamhof, a few doors apart, protected under separate numbers a year apart.

The oaks lie further out: one on a village green in Wutzlhofen, 4 km north-east, and four more beside a field path in Unterisling, 5 km south-east. The Bildeiche, 7.20 metres round, is a separate trip 8 km south near Obertraubling. If you can date any of them, tell us.

faq.q: What is the oldest tree in Regensburg?
faq.a: Of the seven protected entries inside the city on this page, two have an age. The Wutzlhofen Oak was put at about 180 to 200 years by the ordinance that protected it in 1994, so roughly 210 to 230 now, and the Herzogspark plane is put at 150 to 200 years by the tree register baumkunde.de. The others are undated, so one of them could well be older. Just outside the city, the Bildeiche near Obertraubling is estimated at roughly 350 years.

faq.q: Are Regensburg's protected trees free to visit?
faq.a: All eight are free. Four stand on public streets and squares and are reachable at any hour; the Wutzlhofen Oak stands on a village green beside the road; the Unterisling oaks are seen from a public footpath at the edge of a field; the Herzogspark plane is inside a municipal park open during daylight hours; the Bildeiche stands in a meadow beside a public road 8 km south of the city. No ticket is needed anywhere on this list.

faq.q: Can you see the city trees in one walk?
faq.a: The five in the old town and Stadtamhof, yes, in an afternoon. Three are on the old town side, two of them five minutes apart in Prebrunn and one on the Alter Kornmarkt, and the two chestnut groups are over the Steinerne Bruecke in Stadtamhof, a few doors apart on Am Gries. The Wutzlhofen Oak, about 4 km north-east, the Unterisling oaks, about 5 km south-east, and the Bildeiche, 8 km south near Obertraubling, are separate trips.

faq.q: Is one of the chestnuts on Am Gries dying?
faq.a: One of the group was visibly dying when a photographer recorded it on 29 August 2022, and the rest were standing. No more recent public statement about their condition exists. If you see how they are doing now, tell us.

trees.name: The Herzogspark Plane
trees.story:
This plane shares a lawn with a medieval gate tower and is the newcomer of the two by centuries. The Prebrunnturm anchors the northwestern corner of Regensburg's old town, and the ground under both was a bastion in the city wall long before anything was planted on it.

The garden came in 1804, laid out privately for Georg Friedrich von Mueller on the old bastion. The Thurn und Taxis family took it over in 1843, the city bought it in 1935, and it opened to the public between 1950 and 1952 as the Herzogspark.

Where the plane fits into that sequence is not recorded. A photographer's caption from 2022 calls it 200 years old, and the tree register baumkunde.de puts it at 150 to 200. Neither is a ring count, and nothing ties it to the 1804 planting: the park's founding date and the tree's age are two separate facts.

The register did put a tape round it: 6.2 metres round and 31 metres tall on 11 September 2024. The trunk stands on a slope, and the same entry gives 5.85 metres measured on the uphill side, so the girth depends on where you stand.

It is number 10 on the city's own list of natural monuments, one of a small group of Regensburg trees designated individually rather than as part of a landscape. If you know when it went into the ground, tell us.

https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Regensburg-HerzogsparkPlatane-1-Asio.JPG (photographer's own dated description, 29 August 2022: '200-jährige Platane (Naturdenkmal) in dem als Naturdenkmal geschützten Herzogspark')

https://www.baumkunde.de/baumregister/4424-platane_im_herzogspark_regensburg/ (Baumkunde tree register entry 4424: Gewoehnliche Platane, age 150-200, girth 6.2 m measured 11 Sep 2024, 5.85 m measured on the uphill side per its description, height 31.0 m, vital, last visit 11 Sep 2024)
trees.access: Free. Inside the Herzogspark, a public municipal park at the northwestern edge of the Altstadt, open daily during daylight hours.
trees.transport: Regensburg Hauptbahnhof, then about a 15-20 minute walk, or bus to Prebrunn/Herzogspark stop, 5 minute walk.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the plane sharing a lawn with the medieval Prebrunnturm gate tower. It stands in the Herzogspark, at the northwestern edge of Regensburg's old town.

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal Regensburg (Stadt Regensburg, ND-SicherungsVO), no. ND 10

trees.name: The Chestnuts of Am Gries
trees.age_estimate: not documented; mature specimens, one in visible decline as of 2022
trees.story:
One of these chestnuts is dying, and the most recent public look at them was taken four years ago. The photographer who recorded the group on 29 August 2022 captioned the picture with the dying chestnut in the foreground, which remains the only statement anyone has published about their condition. The rest of the group was standing.

Two separate authorities protect them, which is unusual for a row of street trees. Regensburg's own natural monument ordinance lists them as number 52, the Kastanien Am Gries, designated on 28 March 1996. Bavaria's state register carries the same group independently as ND-03369. Between them they establish the species, the position and the protected status. Neither records an age, which is true of almost every tree on this page.

They stand on Am Gries in Stadtamhof, on the far bank of the Danube, about five minutes on foot from the end of the Steinerne Bruecke. That crossing is the reason to do these two chestnut entries together with the old town ones rather than on another day.

Standing in front of them, the group's condition is the thing you will read first. If the failing chestnut has gone since 2022, or if the others have caught up with it, tell us.

Bavaria LfU state Naturdenkmal register, entry ND-03369 'Naturdenkmal Kastanien am Gries, St. Regensburg' (independent state-level designation, coordinates ~250m from the photographed trees, same street)
trees.access: Free. Street trees on Am Gries in Stadtamhof, visible and reachable from the public street.
trees.transport: Across the Steinerne Brücke (Stone Bridge) from the Altstadt, then about a 5 minute walk along Am Gries.
trees.how_to_recognise: The cluster of horse chestnuts on the street outside Am Gries 18, one of them visibly failing as of 2022. The separately protected chestnut at number 30, a few doors east, is a single crown beside a stump.

best_time.label: May, when the white candles stand upright over the whole group

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal Regensburg (Stadt Regensburg, NatDV 52), no. ND 52

trees.name: The Chestnuts of the Golden Lion
trees.story:
The protection here covers one horse chestnut and a torso. That is the register's own wording: entry number 53 on Regensburg's natural monument list, granted on 11 June 1997, protects a single standing chestnut plus what is left of a second, which is a good deal less than the plural in its name suggests.

The name belongs to the building rather than the trees. Zum Goldenen Loewen, the Golden Lion, was an inn on this plot at Am Gries 30, and the chestnut kept the name after the inn stopped trading.

It stands a few doors along from the Kastanien Am Gries, and the two are genuinely separate designations made a year apart under different numbers, not one group counted twice. On the ground the difference is easy: a cluster of trunks outside number 18, a single crown and the remains of its neighbour outside number 30.

Nobody has dated either of them. One city ordinance from 1997 and a photograph from August 2022 are the entire documented record for this tree, and the photograph is also the last confirmation that it is standing. If you know the planting year, or you have five minutes and a tape measure, tell us.
verified_sources: https://www.regensburg.de/stadtrecht/233959/ (city ordinance, 'Rosskastanien Zum Goldenen Loewen in Stadtamhof', Naturdenkmal Nr. 53, designated 11 June 1997)
trees.access: Free. Street trees at Am Gries 30 in Stadtamhof, visible and reachable from the public street; named for the former Zum Goldenen Loewen inn on the same plot.
trees.transport: Across the Steinerne Bruecke (Stone Bridge) from the Altstadt, then about a 5 minute walk along Am Gries.
trees.how_to_recognise: The single horse chestnut outside Am Gries 30, on the plot of the former Zum Goldenen Loewen inn, with the remains of a second tree beside it. The protected group at number 18 is a cluster of several trunks.

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal Regensburg (Stadt Regensburg, NatDV 53), no. ND 53

trees.name: The Plane of the Old Corn Market

location.address: Alter Kornmarkt, Regensburg (south side, near the Alte Kapelle bell tower)
location.neighbourhood: Altstadt (old town, UNESCO World Heritage site)

trees.story:
This plane grows on a market place the Romans laid out around 175 AD. The Alter Kornmarkt is a nearly square open space in the heart of the UNESCO-listed old town, ringed by the Herzogshof, the Roemerturm and the Carmelite monastery, and it has stayed trading ground for most of the time since: a vegetable market still takes it over on Saturday mornings.

The tree is number 34 on the city's list of natural monuments, entered simply as a plane at the Alter Kornmarkt. That entry gives no house number and no coordinate. The square's own description mentions a row of trees along the south side that partly hides the freestanding bell tower of the Alte Kapelle, which is the likeliest place to start looking, though no source actually places this tree in that row. The pin here marks the square rather than a trunk, so expect to spend a minute working out which crown you have come for.

A photograph taken on 11 August 2024 shows it standing. No age has ever been recorded for it, which is ordinary for a tree the city protects by street name and nothing else. If you can date it, or point at the exact trunk, tell us.
verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Regensburg (Naturdenkmal Nr. 34, "Platane", "Am Alten Kornmarkt", designated under the city Naturdenkmal-SicherungsVO)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Naturdenkmal_Platane_am_Alten_Kornmarkt_(Regensburg).jpg (dated photograph, taken 11 August 2024, confirming the tree currently stands)
trees.access: Free. Standing on or beside the Alter Kornmarkt, a public square in the historic centre used for a weekly Saturday vegetable market; open at all times.
trees.transport: In the Altstadt, about a 10 minute walk from Regensburg Hauptbahnhof, next to the Roman-era Roemerturm and Herzogshof.
trees.how_to_recognise: The register gives only the square, so expect to work out which crown you came for. The likeliest place to start is the row along the south side that partly hides the Alte Kapelle's freestanding bell tower.

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal Regensburg (Stadt Regensburg, ND-SicherungsVO), no. ND 34

trees.name: The Plane at Singrün Corner

location.address: Corner of Prebrunnstrasse and Am Singruen, Regensburg

trees.story:
The entry that protects this tree gives no address, only a corner. Number 43 on Regensburg's list of natural monuments is a plane at the corner of Prebrunnstrasse and Am Singrün, and that is the whole of the location anyone has published: no house number, no coordinate, and no GPS tag on the photograph of it either. The pin here marks the corner, which will get you to the right junction and not to the exact trunk.

London planes went into European streets by the thousand for their tolerance of compacted soil and city air, and almost all of them stay anonymous. This one is on the protected list, in Prebrunn on the western edge of the old town, a five minute walk from the plane in the Herzogspark. That proximity makes the two of them a single stop rather than two, which is worth knowing before you plan the afternoon.

The most recent photograph of it was taken on 15 September 2024, which makes this the best confirmed of the five trees here: the others were last recorded in 2022 or 2024. Nobody has dated it, and nobody has put a tape around it. If you can do either, tell us.

https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ND_Platane_am_Singr%C3%BCn_(Regensburg).jpg (dated photograph, taken 15 September 2024, confirming the tree currently stands)
trees.access: Free. Standing at a public street corner in the Prebrunn district, visible and reachable at any time.
trees.transport: About a 10-15 minute walk from Regensburg Hauptbahnhof; a 5 minute walk from the Herzogspark (rgb_001), on the same side of the old town.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by where it stands, on the corner where Prebrunnstrasse meets Am Singruen. The register gives the junction and nothing finer, so the exact trunk is yours to pick out.

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal Regensburg (Stadt Regensburg, ND-SicherungsVO), no. ND 43

trees.name: The Bildeiche at Höhenhof

location.address: Meadow about 600 m south-west of the hamlet Höhenhof, beside the road to Obertraubling, DBU Naturerbe Frauenholz, 93083 Obertraubling

trees.story:
A Madonna stands inside this oak. Long ago a thick limb broke away about a metre above the ground, the wound left a hollow in the trunk, and a figure of the Mother of God was set into it. That is the name: a Bildeiche is an oak with a picture in it. A grille now closes the opening, and there is no other in the trunk.

It is 7.20 metres round, measured in September 2021 by Rainer Lippert, who records Germany's monumental oaks, and 19 metres tall, with a crown built from several heavy limbs going their own way. Lippert puts it at roughly 350 years. That is his estimate, not a ring count, so read it as somewhere between 300 and 400. The tree register baumkunde.de carries the same figures, partly from the same observer, which makes it less of a second opinion than it looks.

Bavaria made it a natural monument on 15 January 1938. The ground around it was military land from 1861 to 2011, a training area from 1958, and Lippert writes that the oak is missing from the literature: a friend of his came across it by chance. Today the meadow belongs to the 494 hectare DBU Naturerbe Frauenholz, the road to Obertraubling runs past, and the tree was last reported in good health in August 2024.

It stands about 8 km south of Regensburg, near Obertraubling. We have not checked the buses, so look up the route before you set out.
trees.access: Stands in a meadow on the DBU Naturerbe Frauenholz (former military training area, managed by Bundesforstbetrieb Hohenfels); baumkunde.de lists access as publicly accessible and the road to Obertraubling passes the tree. The trunk opening with the Madonna figure is behind a grille.
trees.transport: About 8 km south of Regensburg centre, near Obertraubling and Oberhinkofen. We have not checked bus connections or travel time; look up the route before you go.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the grilled hollow about a metre up the trunk, with a Madonna figure inside. It stands on its own in a meadow beside the road to Obertraubling, about 600 m south-west of Höhenhof.

official_register.name: Bavarian LfU Naturdenkmal register ND-02810 (Landkreis Regensburg ND list no. 47)

trees.name: The Wutzlhofen Oak

official_register.name: Stadt Regensburg, Naturdenkmal Nr. 51 (Verordnung vom 4 Feb 1994)

trees.access: Free, always open: stands on the small village green with a fountain and benches in the middle of Wutzlhofen, beside the public road.
trees.transport: Regensburg city bus to Wutzlhofen; line and stop not verified, so unchecked. About 4 km north-east of the old town.
trees.story:
Regensburg protects this oak for being the middle of a village. The ordinance that made it natural monument number 51 on 4 February 1994 says so in as many words: the oak is to be kept as the centre of Wutzlhofen, for its outstanding beauty and its age.

The same ordinance put that age at about 180 to 200 years in 1994. Carried forward, that makes it somewhere past two centuries now, roughly 210 to 230, though it is the city's own round figure and not a ring count. Either way the oak was already more than a hundred years old in 1924, when Wutzlhofen became part of Regensburg.

The place is far older than the tree. Wutzlhofen first appears in 1224 as Wuzenhoven, a property of the Regensburg cathedral chapter. The oak's protection reaches 11 metres out from the middle of its trunk, and around it is a small green with a fountain, five benches and two seesaw animals, opposite house number 42, about 4 km north-east of the old town.

It is no champion. It is a village tree doing the job the village gave it. The city still listed it in 2020, and we have found no dated photograph since. Nobody has published its girth, its height or which oak it is. If you know, tell us.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the oak on Wutzlhofen's small village green, with a fountain and benches close by. It stands beside the road, opposite house number 42.

trees.name: The Unterisling Oaks

location.address: Stadlerstrasse (east of no. 11), Papstwiese / Islinger Feld, 93053 Regensburg

official_register.name: Stadt Regensburg, Naturdenkmal Nr. 50 (Verordnung vom 26 May 1993)

trees.access: Free. The four oaks stand beside a public footway (OSM way 28290618: highway=footway, access=yes, foot=yes) at the edge of the Islinger Feld meadow (OSM landuse=meadow). Trees are on a field plot; view from the path.
trees.transport: South-east of the old town in Unterisling, about 5 km from the centre; bus line and stop not verified, so unchecked.
trees.story:
Regensburg protects these four oaks as one monument, and the field around them with them. City ordinance number 50, signed on 26 May 1993, covers the four trees and about 1,400 square metres of the plot they stand on, at the edge of the Islinger Feld meadow in Unterisling. The city's list calls the spot the Papstwiese, the Pope's meadow.

The ordinance gives three reasons: their outstanding beauty, their age, and the way they shape the look of the village. It does not say what that age is, and nothing else we have found does either. There is no girth, no height and no planting date for any of the four, which makes them the least documented trees on this page and a clean example of Regensburg protecting a tree without measuring it.

They were standing on 19 April 2024, when a naturalist photographed them and logged them as pedunculate oaks. Nobody has confirmed that guess, so here they are simply oaks.

A public footpath runs past them, and the trees themselves stand on a field plot, so these are oaks to see from the path rather than to walk under. The four trunks are spread over about 45 metres, close enough to take in from one place. If you know which oak they are, or how old, tell us.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise them as four oaks standing together, spread over about 45 metres at the edge of the Islinger Feld meadow. They stand beside the public footpath east of Stadlerstrasse 11.
